dataset: Bio-AI Centre of Excellence — Arogyamithran Quiz Bank
description: 100 source-linked English multiple-choice questions for a visitor quiz. Review wording and references before production. Ten unique questions should be selected server-side per attempt.

selection_policy.recommended_repeat_visitor_policy: Track question IDs shown per visitor using an opaque visitor ID; prioritise unseen questions. When fewer than 10 unseen questions remain, either ask permission to recycle or reset history according to organiser policy.
selection_policy.security: Do not send correct_option_index or correct_answer to the browser before the answer is submitted. Validate and score on the server.

questions.question: The word 'Ayurveda' is commonly explained from which Sanskrit words?
questions.correct_answer: Ayus (life) and Veda (knowledge)
questions.explanation: Ayurveda is commonly glossed as the knowledge or science of life. This describes the traditional system's name, not proof of a treatment claim.

questions.question: Which set is traditionally known as the three doshas in Ayurveda?
questions.correct_answer: Vata, Pitta and Kapha
questions.explanation: Vata, Pitta and Kapha are central concepts in traditional Ayurvedic theory.

questions.question: Which plant part is the usual culinary source of turmeric powder?
questions.correct_answer: Rhizome
questions.explanation: Turmeric powder is made from the rhizome, an underground stem, of Curcuma longa.

questions.question: Which scientific name is associated with Ashwagandha?
questions.correct_answer: Withania somnifera
questions.explanation: Withania somnifera is the botanical name used for Ashwagandha.

questions.question: Amla is commonly identified botanically as which species?
questions.correct_answer: Phyllanthus emblica
questions.explanation: Amla or Indian gooseberry is Phyllanthus emblica; some references use the synonym Emblica officinalis.

questions.question: Which three fruits are traditionally combined in Triphala?
questions.correct_answer: Amla, Haritaki and Bibhitaki
questions.explanation: Triphala traditionally combines Phyllanthus emblica, Terminalia chebula and Terminalia bellirica.

questions.question: Neem's accepted scientific name is which of these?
questions.correct_answer: Azadirachta indica
questions.explanation: Azadirachta indica is neem. Common names should be checked against scientific names to avoid confusion.

questions.question: Which plant is commonly called Shatavari?
questions.correct_answer: Asparagus racemosus
questions.explanation: Asparagus racemosus is widely referred to as Shatavari in Indian traditional plant resources.

questions.question: Which statement about an Ayurvedic traditional use is most accurate?
options: A traditional use automatically proves clinical effectiveness
Traditional use is historical/contextual information; efficacy needs evidence for the specific claim
All traditional plants are safe at any dose
A plant name alone establishes the correct dose
questions.correct_answer: Traditional use is historical/contextual information; efficacy needs evidence for the specific claim
questions.explanation: Traditional use and modern evidence are different kinds of information. Specific health claims need appropriate evidence and safety review.

questions.question: Which plant is commonly associated with the Ayurvedic name Guduchi/Giloy?
questions.correct_answer: Tinospora cordifolia
questions.explanation: Tinospora cordifolia is commonly called Guduchi or Giloy in Indian medicinal-plant resources.

questions.question: The plant part most commonly described for Yashtimadhu/licorice is its…
questions.correct_answer: Root
questions.explanation: Glycyrrhiza glabra root is used in licorice products. Concentrated use can have important safety concerns.

questions.question: Which best describes a 'rasayana' in traditional Ayurveda?
options: A category of rejuvenation/healthy-ageing concepts in Ayurvedic texts
questions.correct_answer: A category of rejuvenation/healthy-ageing concepts in Ayurvedic texts
questions.explanation: Rasayana is a traditional Ayurvedic concept often associated with rejuvenation and maintaining vitality; exact meanings vary by text and context.

questions.question: What should a visitor do before using an unfamiliar medicinal plant for a health problem?
options: Assume it is safe because it is natural
Identify it accurately and consult a qualified healthcare professional
questions.correct_answer: Identify it accurately and consult a qualified healthcare professional
questions.explanation: Correct identification, known safety information and professional advice matter; natural origin does not guarantee safety.

questions.question: Brahmi is a common name associated with which plant in many Indian references?
questions.correct_answer: Bacopa monnieri
questions.explanation: Bacopa monnieri is often called Brahmi, although common-name usage can vary by region and species.

questions.question: Which plant is associated with the Ayurvedic name Arjuna?
questions.correct_answer: Terminalia arjuna
questions.explanation: Terminalia arjuna is the species commonly called Arjuna. Its traditional context should not be mistaken for a proven treatment recommendation.

questions.question: Why should the scientific name accompany a medicinal plant's common name?
options: Common names are always unique worldwide
The same common name may refer to different species
Scientific names give a guaranteed dosage
It proves the product is authentic
questions.correct_answer: The same common name may refer to different species
questions.explanation: Kew's medicinal plant name resources note that common names can be ambiguous and taxonomic identity needs to be checked.

questions.question: Which plant is known as Vasaka/Adhatoda in some Indian medicinal plant references?
questions.correct_answer: Justicia adhatoda
questions.explanation: Justicia adhatoda, also known in older references as Adhatoda vasica, is commonly called Vasaka.

questions.question: What is the safest interpretation of an herb's place in Ayurveda?
options: It is guaranteed to cure the condition mentioned in old text
Its use is part of a traditional knowledge system, while modern safety and efficacy require separate evaluation
It never interacts with other products
questions.correct_answer: Its use is part of a traditional knowledge system, while modern safety and efficacy require separate evaluation
questions.explanation: Traditional context should be presented respectfully but separately from evidence of effectiveness and product safety.

questions.question: Which plant is traditionally called Haritaki?
questions.correct_answer: Terminalia chebula
questions.explanation: Terminalia chebula is commonly known as Haritaki or Harad.

questions.question: Which is a good VedaVerse content practice?
options: Show traditional uses, research evidence, limitations and safety notes separately
questions.correct_answer: Show traditional uses, research evidence, limitations and safety notes separately
questions.explanation: Separating traditions, evidence, uncertainty and safety helps visitors learn without being misled.

questions.question: Which part of the black pepper plant is used as the spice?
questions.correct_answer: Fruit
questions.explanation: Black pepper is made from fruits of Piper nigrum.

questions.question: Which spice is the unopened flower bud of Syzygium aromaticum?
questions.correct_answer: Clove
questions.explanation: Cloves are dried unopened flower buds.

questions.question: Saffron is collected from which part of Crocus sativus?
questions.correct_answer: Stigmas
questions.explanation: Saffron consists of the dried red stigmas of Crocus sativus.

questions.question: Nutmeg and mace come from…
options: Different parts of the fruit of Myristica fragrans
The root and leaves of ginger
questions.correct_answer: Different parts of the fruit of Myristica fragrans
questions.explanation: Nutmeg is the seed kernel, while mace is the aril around it.

questions.question: Which spice is derived from the bark of Cinnamomum verum?
questions.correct_answer: Ceylon cinnamon
questions.explanation: Ceylon cinnamon is produced from the bark of Cinnamomum verum.

questions.question: Which spice comes from the rhizome of Zingiber officinale?
questions.correct_answer: Ginger
questions.explanation: Ginger is the underground rhizome of Zingiber officinale.

questions.question: Turmeric's botanical name is…
questions.correct_answer: Curcuma longa
questions.explanation: Curcuma longa is turmeric; Kew describes its rhizomes as the source of the spice.

questions.question: Which plant gives us green/small cardamom?
questions.correct_answer: Elettaria cardamomum
questions.explanation: Elettaria cardamomum is small cardamom, native to southwest India.

questions.question: Which spice is commonly called 'malli' in Malayalam?
questions.correct_answer: Coriander
questions.explanation: Malli commonly refers to coriander in Malayalam; leaves and dried fruits are used in cooking.

questions.question: Which spice is known as 'jeerakam' in Malayalam?
questions.correct_answer: Cumin
questions.explanation: Jeerakam is the common Malayalam name for cumin.

questions.question: The spice part commonly called a cinnamon stick is usually…
questions.correct_answer: Bark
questions.explanation: Cinnamon sticks are rolled pieces of inner bark.

questions.question: Which spice comes from a pod of an orchid?
questions.correct_answer: Vanilla
questions.explanation: Vanilla planifolia is an orchid whose cured fruit pods provide vanilla flavour.

questions.question: Which spice comes from the fruit of Illicium verum?
questions.correct_answer: Star anise
questions.explanation: Chinese star anise is the star-shaped fruit of Illicium verum.

questions.question: Which leaf is commonly used to season Kerala curries and is called kariveppila?
questions.correct_answer: Curry leaf
questions.explanation: Kariveppila is curry leaf, commonly identified with Bergera koenigii (syn. Murraya koenigii).

questions.question: Which two culinary spices come from the same species, Myristica fragrans?
questions.correct_answer: Nutmeg and mace
questions.explanation: Nutmeg is the seed kernel and mace is its surrounding aril.

questions.question: Asafoetida used in cooking is primarily what type of plant product?
questions.correct_answer: Oleo-gum-resin
questions.explanation: The Spices Board list describes asafoetida as an oleo-gum-resin.

questions.question: Kokum used as a souring agent comes from which plant?
questions.correct_answer: Garcinia indica
questions.explanation: Garcinia indica fruit rind is used as a souring ingredient in regional dishes.

questions.question: Which spice is commonly called 'thippali' in Malayalam?
questions.correct_answer: Long pepper
questions.explanation: Thippali is long pepper, Piper longum.

questions.question: Which one is a legume whose seeds are used as a spice and whose leaves are also eaten?
questions.correct_answer: Fenugreek
questions.explanation: Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is a legume used for both seeds and leaves.

questions.question: Why must culinary basil and holy basil/tulsi not automatically be treated as the same species?
options: All plants have identical scientific names
They can refer to different species despite similar common names
questions.correct_answer: They can refer to different species despite similar common names
questions.explanation: Sweet basil is commonly Ocimum basilicum; holy basil is commonly Ocimum tenuiflorum (often cited as O. sanctum). Common names can overlap.

questions.question: What molecule carries most inherited genetic information in living organisms?
questions.correct_answer: DNA
questions.explanation: DNA stores hereditary information in most organisms.

questions.question: What does DNA stand for?
questions.correct_answer: Deoxyribonucleic acid
questions.explanation: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid.

questions.question: Which molecule is commonly involved in carrying genetic instructions from DNA to protein-making machinery?
questions.correct_answer: RNA
questions.explanation: Messenger RNA carries coding information used during protein synthesis.

questions.question: What is a genome?
options: An organism's complete set of genetic material
questions.correct_answer: An organism's complete set of genetic material
questions.explanation: A genome is the complete set of genetic material for an organism or biological entity.

questions.question: Bioinformatics combines biology with…
questions.correct_answer: Computing and data analysis
questions.explanation: Bioinformatics uses computational and statistical methods to analyse biological data.

questions.question: Artificial intelligence is best described as…
options: Computing methods that perform tasks associated with human-like intelligence
questions.correct_answer: Computing methods that perform tasks associated with human-like intelligence
questions.explanation: AI refers broadly to computational systems that perform tasks such as pattern recognition, prediction or language processing.

questions.question: Machine learning is generally considered…
options: A subset of AI that learns patterns from data
questions.correct_answer: A subset of AI that learns patterns from data
questions.explanation: Machine learning is a branch of AI that uses data to fit models or identify patterns.

questions.question: What is the basic structural unit of living organisms?
questions.correct_answer: Cell
questions.explanation: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of living organisms.

questions.question: What is the main role of DNA sequencing?
options: Determining the order of DNA bases
questions.correct_answer: Determining the order of DNA bases
questions.explanation: DNA sequencing determines the order of nucleotides in a DNA molecule.

questions.question: Which set lists the four common DNA bases?
questions.correct_answer: A, C, G and T
questions.explanation: DNA uses adenine, cytosine, guanine and thymine.

questions.question: Proteins are built from smaller units called…
questions.correct_answer: Amino acids
questions.explanation: Amino acids are linked to form proteins.

questions.question: What is an enzyme?
questions.correct_answer: A biological catalyst
questions.explanation: Enzymes speed up biochemical reactions without being consumed in the overall reaction.

questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to see cells too small for the naked eye?
questions.correct_answer: Microscope
questions.explanation: Microscopes make small structures such as cells visible at suitable magnification.

questions.question: What does PCR do in molecular biology?
questions.correct_answer: Amplifies selected DNA sequences
questions.explanation: Polymerase chain reaction makes many copies of a selected DNA region.

questions.question: A biosensor is designed to…
options: Detect a biological or chemical target and convert it into a measurable signal
questions.correct_answer: Detect a biological or chemical target and convert it into a measurable signal
questions.explanation: Biosensors use a recognition element and a transducer to detect a target and produce a measurable signal.

questions.question: What is the role of a cell membrane?
options: It forms a boundary and helps regulate exchange with the environment
It is made only of wood
questions.correct_answer: It forms a boundary and helps regulate exchange with the environment
questions.explanation: Cell membranes form selective boundaries around cells and regulate material exchange.

questions.question: Which is a microorganism?
questions.correct_answer: A bacterium
questions.explanation: Bacteria are microscopic single-celled organisms; different bacteria have different effects and uses.

questions.question: Why is a virus not classified as a typical free-living cell?
options: It requires host-cell machinery to reproduce
It is always larger than a tree
questions.correct_answer: It requires host-cell machinery to reproduce
questions.explanation: Viruses use host cells to reproduce and are not made of the same cellular structures as bacteria.

questions.question: What is fermentation commonly used for in food production?
options: Microorganisms transform ingredients into products such as yoghurt or fermented vegetables
It removes every molecule from food
It converts all foods into plastic
It stops all biological activity permanently
questions.correct_answer: Microorganisms transform ingredients into products such as yoghurt or fermented vegetables
questions.explanation: Fermentation uses microbial activity to change foods, often affecting flavour, texture and preservation.

questions.question: Why can AI be useful in analysing biological datasets?
options: It can help detect patterns in large datasets, but results need validation
It guarantees every scientific conclusion is correct
It removes the need for data quality
It proves a traditional treatment works automatically
questions.correct_answer: It can help detect patterns in large datasets, but results need validation
questions.explanation: AI can support analysis and prediction, but methods, data quality, bias and results require expert validation.

questions.question: What does biodiversity refer to?
options: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
Only the number of trees in one garden
questions.correct_answer: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes diversity within species, between species and across ecosystems.

questions.question: What is a herbarium?
options: A collection of preserved, documented plant specimens
questions.correct_answer: A collection of preserved, documented plant specimens
questions.explanation: Herbaria preserve labelled plant specimens used in identification and research.

questions.question: Why are scientific names useful in a plant database?
options: They help distinguish species across languages and common-name systems
They tell the dose to take
They remove the need for identification
questions.correct_answer: They help distinguish species across languages and common-name systems
questions.explanation: Scientific names support consistent identification, although taxonomy and synonyms still need review.

questions.question: What is a pollinator?
options: An organism that transfers pollen between flowers
questions.correct_answer: An organism that transfers pollen between flowers
questions.explanation: Pollinators such as bees and some birds or bats help transfer pollen in flowering plants.

questions.question: Which is an example of ex-situ conservation?
options: Maintaining seeds in a seed bank
Protecting a species only in its natural forest
questions.correct_answer: Maintaining seeds in a seed bank
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation maintains components of biodiversity outside their natural habitats, such as in seed banks or botanical gardens.

questions.question: Which is an example of in-situ conservation?
options: Protecting a species in its natural habitat
Keeping a seed packet in a freezer only
Photographing a plant and discarding it
questions.correct_answer: Protecting a species in its natural habitat
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species within their ecosystems and natural habitats.

questions.question: What is an invasive alien species?
options: A non-native species that establishes and causes or may cause harm
questions.correct_answer: A non-native species that establishes and causes or may cause harm
questions.explanation: Invasive alien species can threaten biodiversity, ecosystem functioning or human interests.

questions.question: What does sustainable harvesting aim to do?
options: Collect resources in a way that allows populations and ecosystems to persist
Remove seeds before they reproduce every time
questions.correct_answer: Collect resources in a way that allows populations and ecosystems to persist
questions.explanation: Sustainable harvesting considers regeneration, habitat impact and long-term availability.

questions.question: Why should rare wild medicinal plants be sourced carefully?
options: Overharvesting can threaten wild populations and habitats
Wild plants are always more effective
Only rare plants have scientific names
questions.correct_answer: Overharvesting can threaten wild populations and habitats
questions.explanation: Demand and unsustainable collection can damage wild populations; traceable, cultivated sources may help reduce pressure.

questions.question: What does a plant family represent in taxonomy?
questions.correct_answer: A grouping of related genera
questions.explanation: Plant families group related genera and help describe relationships among plants.

questions.question: Which part of a plant is commonly associated with seed dispersal?
options: The stem's xylem in every species
questions.correct_answer: Fruit in many flowering plants
questions.explanation: In flowering plants, fruits often protect seeds and help disperse them, though mechanisms vary widely.

questions.question: Which plant structure usually absorbs water and minerals from soil?
questions.correct_answer: Roots
questions.explanation: Roots commonly anchor plants and absorb water and mineral nutrients.

questions.question: What is photosynthesis?
options: A process using light energy to help make sugars from carbon dioxide and water
The breakdown of DNA by AI
questions.correct_answer: A process using light energy to help make sugars from carbon dioxide and water
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy; plants use carbon dioxide and water to produce sugars and release oxygen in oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.question: Why is preserving a botanical voucher specimen valuable in research?
options: It provides a documented physical reference for plant identity
It guarantees a medicinal claim is true
questions.correct_answer: It provides a documented physical reference for plant identity
questions.explanation: Voucher specimens allow later researchers to check which organism was studied.

questions.question: What is a seed bank primarily used for?
options: Storing seeds under controlled conditions for conservation and research
Producing all plant species in one day
questions.correct_answer: Storing seeds under controlled conditions for conservation and research
questions.explanation: Seed banks preserve seed diversity for future conservation, research or restoration, depending on the species and storage method.

questions.question: Why should a medicinal plant record include its plant part used?
options: Different plant parts can have different chemistry and safety profiles
Every part always has the same effect
It guarantees the plant is sustainable
questions.correct_answer: Different plant parts can have different chemistry and safety profiles
questions.explanation: Part identity matters because leaves, roots, bark, fruit and seeds can differ in composition and risk.

questions.question: What is one reason biodiversity matters to agriculture?
options: It supports genetic resources, pollination, soil function and resilience
It eliminates pests in every case
It removes the need to conserve water
questions.correct_answer: It supports genetic resources, pollination, soil function and resilience
questions.explanation: Biodiversity contributes to ecosystem services that support agricultural production and resilience.

questions.question: What is a native species?
options: A species that occurs naturally in a particular region
A species always imported from another continent
questions.correct_answer: A species that occurs naturally in a particular region
questions.explanation: Native species occur naturally in a region without being introduced there by people.

questions.question: Why should the common name and scientific name both be displayed on VedaVerse?
options: It is easier to explore in local language while keeping species identity clearer
The common name proves the right dose
The scientific name is always written in Malayalam
One of the names should be fake
questions.correct_answer: It is easier to explore in local language while keeping species identity clearer
questions.explanation: Using both names helps visitors while reducing ambiguity caused by common names.

questions.question: A plant's conservation status should be…
options: Taken from a reliable, current source and shown with its source/date
Guessed from how attractive it looks
questions.correct_answer: Taken from a reliable, current source and shown with its source/date
questions.explanation: Conservation status needs a credible source and should match the exact species and assessment date.

questions.question: Does 'natural' automatically mean a product is safe?
options: Yes, all natural products are harmless
No; natural products can have side effects, interactions or toxins
questions.correct_answer: No; natural products can have side effects, interactions or toxins
questions.explanation: Natural substances can be harmful, toxic, contaminated or interact with medicines; product and dose matter.

questions.question: What does a peer-reviewed research paper generally mean?
options: Other experts assessed the work before publication
The result is guaranteed to be true forever
The study was conducted by a plant
questions.correct_answer: Other experts assessed the work before publication
questions.explanation: Peer review is a quality-control step, not a guarantee that every finding is correct.

questions.question: What is a clinical study designed to investigate?
options: Questions involving people, such as safety or effects of an intervention
Only the colour of a laboratory wall
Whether a common name is popular
questions.correct_answer: Questions involving people, such as safety or effects of an intervention
questions.explanation: Clinical studies involving people investigate health-related questions under defined protocols and oversight.

questions.question: If a compound changes cells in a laboratory dish, does that prove a plant cures a disease in people?
options: No; laboratory findings need further testing and do not establish clinical benefit
Only if the plant is green
Yes, if the result is posted online
questions.correct_answer: No; laboratory findings need further testing and do not establish clinical benefit
questions.explanation: In-vitro results are early evidence and do not automatically translate into safe or effective treatment in humans.

questions.question: Why should medicinal products be checked for interactions with prescribed medicines?
options: Plants and supplements can change medicine effects or risks
It is needed only for spices in food
It proves all medicines are unnecessary
questions.correct_answer: Plants and supplements can change medicine effects or risks
questions.explanation: Some herbal products affect drug metabolism, bleeding, blood pressure or other outcomes, so interactions need review.

questions.question: What should you do if a herbal product causes a severe or unexpected reaction?
options: Stop using it and seek appropriate medical advice promptly
questions.correct_answer: Stop using it and seek appropriate medical advice promptly
questions.explanation: Unexpected or severe reactions deserve prompt professional evaluation; emergencies require urgent care.

questions.question: Why are standardised names and quality checks important for herbs?
options: They reduce confusion, substitution, contamination and variability
questions.correct_answer: They reduce confusion, substitution, contamination and variability
questions.explanation: Correct identity and quality controls help reduce adulteration, contamination and variation in herbal products.

questions.question: What should a quiz explanation do when evidence is uncertain?
options: State uncertainty clearly and avoid overstating a claim
questions.correct_answer: State uncertainty clearly and avoid overstating a claim
questions.explanation: Good science communication explains the limits of the evidence rather than presenting uncertainty as certainty.

questions.question: Which source is most appropriate for checking an accepted botanical name?
options: A recognised botanical database such as Kew Plants of the World Online
questions.correct_answer: A recognised botanical database such as Kew Plants of the World Online
questions.explanation: Kew's Plants of the World Online is a recognised resource for checking plant taxonomy and accepted names.

questions.question: What is the safest policy for a visitor who wants treatment advice from Arogyamithran?
options: Explain it is educational and recommend a qualified healthcare professional
Tell them to stop prescribed medicine
questions.correct_answer: Explain it is educational and recommend a qualified healthcare professional
questions.explanation: Arogyamithran should be an educational guide, not a diagnosis or prescribing service.

questions.question: Why should a plant record cite the source of its traditional-use description?
options: It lets readers check the context and avoid unsourced claims
It makes the plant more potent
It means the source endorses every use
It removes the need for safety information
questions.correct_answer: It lets readers check the context and avoid unsourced claims
questions.explanation: References help visitors and reviewers verify claims and distinguish documentation from endorsement.

questions.question: What does the presence of a WHO medicinal-plant monograph mean?
options: WHO has guaranteed that every use is effective
The monograph compiles information about a plant; it is not blanket endorsement of every use
The plant is harmless in any dose
questions.correct_answer: The monograph compiles information about a plant; it is not blanket endorsement of every use
questions.explanation: WHO describes its monographs as information on safety, efficacy and quality, not as automatic official endorsement of every medicinal use.

questions.question: Why should a plant be identified by a qualified source before it is consumed?
options: Similar-looking species may have different properties or may be toxic
Every plant in a forest is edible
questions.correct_answer: Similar-looking species may have different properties or may be toxic
questions.explanation: Lookalike plants may differ substantially in safety; reliable identification is essential.

questions.question: Which is a responsible way to present turmeric research?
options: Describe the specific research and limitations, and distinguish food use from supplements
Assume concentrated extracts are identical to food
questions.correct_answer: Describe the specific research and limitations, and distinguish food use from supplements
questions.explanation: NCCIH describes traditional uses and notes that research and supplement safety vary; claims should be specific and proportionate.

questions.question: Why should an herbal supplement's ingredients and label be checked?
options: Products can vary in composition and may contain other ingredients or contaminants
Labels always prove the contents are correct
It is only needed for fruits
questions.correct_answer: Products can vary in composition and may contain other ingredients or contaminants
questions.explanation: Quality and identity can vary, so transparent labels and reliable manufacturing sources matter.

questions.question: What should the public leaderboard display?
options: Only permitted display names and scores
questions.correct_answer: Only permitted display names and scores
questions.explanation: Public rankings should minimise personal data and never expose phone numbers or unrelated private details.

questions.question: When should Arogyamithran claim that a score has been saved?
options: Immediately after the visitor taps Submit, even if the server failed
Only after the application receives successful confirmation from persistence
questions.correct_answer: Only after the application receives successful confirmation from persistence
questions.explanation: The interface must report persistence honestly and show retry/error behaviour when saving fails.

questions.question: What is the best use of AI in a plant knowledge app?
options: Help search and organise verified content while sources and limitations remain visible
questions.correct_answer: Help search and organise verified content while sources and limitations remain visible
questions.explanation: AI can support information retrieval, but factual claims and plant identity still require reliable data and validation.

questions.question: What should happen when a plant profile has not been reviewed?
options: Mark it as awaiting review and avoid unsupported claims
questions.correct_answer: Mark it as awaiting review and avoid unsupported claims
questions.explanation: Review status should be visible internally, and unverified health claims should not be presented as established facts.

questions.question: Which is the best rule for essential oils in a visitor education app?
options: Tell users to drink them directly
Explain they are concentrated products and not equivalent to the whole herb or food spice
Say every oil is safe for all ages
questions.correct_answer: Explain they are concentrated products and not equivalent to the whole herb or food spice
questions.explanation: Essential oils are concentrated and have different exposure and safety profiles from culinary herbs; ingestion can be dangerous.
